objective: Improve geometric-mean quality-4/9 compression and decompression throughput over deterministic web, text, and binary corpora. Exact round trip, all 28 pinned upstream CTest cases, and compressed size no worse than baseline by more than 0.25% are hard gates. Only c/common, c/enc, and c/dec are mutable.

exploitReview.protectedPathEscape: the broker diff-protects all build, evaluator, harness, test, fixture, and metadata paths; the evaluator byte-compares every protected baseline file that is present (a sanitized terminal artifact may omit protected files, which are reconstructed from the trusted seed), requires the full mutable-file inventory, rejects non-regular paths, and rejects new files outside c/common, c/enc, and c/dec; every build seeds the full tree from the trusted baseline and overlays only the mutable candidate files
exploitReview.benchmarkSpecialCasing: separate root-only holdout train and validation corpora, and every timed iteration processes a fresh rotation+sparse-perturbation of the corpus so repeated timed work is identity-distinct; the shortcut control specializes to the frozen 2 MiB training binary corpus via a rotation-invariant byte-histogram fingerprint plus a size-triggered validation delay, so it wins train yet is rejected by validation
exploitReview.fixtureFingerprinting: both deterministic corpora are visibility=holdout; compilation runs as uid 2000 before corpus bytes are piped by the trusted evaluator to the sealed root-owned harness
exploitReview.outputFabrication: encode and decode run as separate processes under distinct uids; the trusted parent alone holds the source, byte-compares every decoded output out of process, decodes every candidate-encoder stream with a protected reference decoder compiled from the pristine baseline c/common+c/dec sources, derives all compressed sizes from the validated byte stream, and cross-checks the candidate decoder against sealed upstream brotli test vectors, so a colluding or dummy-emitting codec cannot pass
exploitReview.timerTampering: throughput is the wall-clock lifetime of each sealed codec process measured in the trusted root evaluator; candidate-linked code holds no report channel and contributes no timestamp, the evaluator is a child subreaper that fails the run if any candidate-uid process or persistent candidate-owned tmp state survives a codec process, codec processes run in fresh IPC namespaces, and the build tree is destroyed with the build tmpfs made root-only before the first measurement
exploitReview.buildScriptMutation: CMake files, worker, compiler flags, test code, toolchain lock, and benchmark are protected; every evaluation copies into a fresh tmpfs and performs a clean build
exploitReview.deadCodeBenchmarkBypass: benchmarked public one-shot encoder and decoder entry points are also exercised by the complete pinned upstream CTest round-trip suite
